plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and reduce overall exposure.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim SMH to 5% as it is flagged for trimming.
Sell QQQ as it is flagged for selling and in a downtrend.
Sell SMCI as it is flagged below its stop.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5% monthly return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns. However, potential upside is also limited.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Reduce SOXL to 3% and MUU to 1% to lower leveraged ETF exposure.
Sell SPAL as it is flagged below its stop.
Trim SMH to 5% as it is flagged for trimming.
Sell QQQ as it is flagged for selling and in a downtrend.
Buy XLV at 4% as a strong scanner setup to diversify.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly growth with a risk-first approach. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality new setup. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Add to SOXL and MUU, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged exposure.
Sell SPAL as it is flagged below its stop.
Trim SMH to 5% as it is flagged for trimming.
Sell QQQ as it is flagged for selling and in a downtrend.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for ~4% monthly growth by leveraging high-conviction setups. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs, which can lead to substantial drawdowns and daily decay. Strict stop discipline is critical to manage the elevated risk.

plan: Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase income exposure.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Sell SMH and CRWD to reduce high-beta single name exposure.
Sell QQQ as it is flagged for selling and in a downtrend.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly distributions, prioritizing yield and low drawdown. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets. While aiming for steady income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
